name: Bhramari · humming bee breath
summary: A soft in-breath, then a long, even hum on the out-breath, with the lips closed, so the vibration fills the skull. Then sit in the silence after the sound.

steps.text: Sit upright, lips closed, teeth slightly apart, jaw soft. Optionally close the ears with the thumbs.
Breathe out slowly with a steady, low hum. Feel it vibrate through the head.
Repeat 5–9 times, then sit in the silence and listen inward.

contraindications: Ear infection: don't close the ears.
Keep it gentle; no breath holding in this version.

intro.caption: Lips closed, teeth apart, jaw soft. Thumbs may close the ears.

round.caption: Breathe in softly through the nose.

round.label: Hum
round.caption: Hum… a steady, low “mmm”. Feel the skull vibrate.

outro.caption: Hands down. Sit in the silence after the sound.

sources.cite: Haṭha Yoga Pradīpikā 2.68 (tr. Pancham Singh): breathe in briskly with a bee-like sound, breathe out slowly humming; bliss arises in the mind
Swami Sivananda, The Science of Pranayama, ch. 3 'Bhramari': a faster bee-sound variant ending in a comfortable kumbhaka (not used here)

meta.confidence_note: The engine uses the common modern form: a quiet inhale and a hum on the exhale only. HYP 2.68 sounds the bee on both breaths, and Sivananda's version is rapid and ends in a hold. Optional ear closing (shanmukhi) and the 4:9 pacing are ours.
